chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abu Ishaq al-Khurasani, who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was saying: 'Beware of lying, for every hopeful one is a seeker, and every fearful one is a fugitive.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and psychological significance of avoiding lies according to Imam Ali in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) links the act of lying to the fundamental human psychological states of hope and fear, suggesting that deception is often a strategic tool for those seeking gain or avoiding peril. This insight is central to Shia ethical teachings, emphasizing that truthfulness is not merely a moral duty but a reflection of inner spiritual stability and clarity of purpose.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Abu Is’haq Al Khurasany who said,
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws was saying: ‘Beware of the lie, for every hopeful one seeks, and every fearful one flees’.
en.sarwar: 21. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from abu Ishaq al-Khurasani who has said the following: “
Amir al-Mifminin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) would say, ‘Beware of lying; every hopeful strives to make his wish come true and every fearful person runs away (and I do not find this quality in you).”
